newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower, and feeder cattle were called steady, analysts said.

Although a few head of cash cattle traded at $68 per cwt Tuesday and some analysts look for cattle to trade at $69 or better, most analysts see the cash market working lower into June and pressuring live cattle futures. Boxed beef values have weakened and this will be weighing on packer demand after this week, they said.
Friday's Cattle-on-Feed report is also expected to show larger than year ago on feed supplies, they said.
Analysts' estimates for May 1 on-feed numbers ranged from 108 to 111 percent of last year. Placement estimates ranged from 104.9 to 127.5 and marketings 98.6 to 104 percent.

Feeder futures were expected to open steady after slipping Tuesday on profit taking. Although some analysts look for further profit taking and pressure from expected higher CBOT corn futures, others cited continued good demand for heavier-weight replacement feeders and the rising CME feeder cattle index.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.68 to $75.97 per cwt, highest level since Jan 26, 1995.
